hints.content: Increasing at a rate of $6.7\%$ means the per capita GDP keeps its $100\%$ and adds $6.7\%$ more, for a total of $106.7\%$.
So each year, the per capita GDP is multiplied by $106.7\%$, which is the same as a factor of $1.067$.

If we start with the initial per capita GDP, $\$1800$, and keep multiplying by $1.067$, this function gives us the approximate per capita GDP $G(t)$ of Australia $t$ years after $1950$:

$G(t)=1800\cdot1.067^t$

question.content:
